==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|remote}}, from {{der|en|fro|remot}}, masculine, {{m|fro|remote}}, feminine, from {{der|en|la|remotus}}, past participle of {{m|la|removere||to remove}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|movere||to move}}.

===Adjective===

# At a [[distance]]; [[disconnected]].

#: {{syn|en|far|hidden|Thesaurus:distant}}
#: {{ant|en|close|near|proximate|Thesaurus:near}}
#: {{ux|en|After his fall from the emperor's favor, the general was posted to a '''remote''' outpost.}}
# {{lb|en|especially with respect to [[likelihood]]}} [[slight|Slight]].
#: {{syn|en|distant|faint|small}}
#: {{ant|en|considerable|great|reasonable|sure}}
#: {{ux|en|There was only a '''remote''' possibility that we would be rescued as we were far outside of the regular shipping lanes.}}

#: {{ux|en|You have a '''remote''' resemblance to my grandmother.}}
# [[emotion|Emotionally]] [[detach]]ed.
#: {{syn|en|aloof|dispassionate|distant|removed|withdrawn|Thesaurus:aloof}}
#: {{ant|en|companionable|intimate|involved|passionate}}
#: {{ux|en|After her mother's death, my friend grew '''remote''' for a time while she dealt with her grief.}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰedʰ-|id1=bend|*bʰeydʰ-}}
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:badde|tree=+}}
From {{inh|en|enm|bad}}, {{m|enm|badde|t=wicked, evil, depraved}}, of {{unk|en|title=uncertain}} origin. Perhaps a shortening of {{der|en|ang|bæddel||hermaphrodite}} (for loss of ''-el'' compare {{m+|enm|muche}} from {{m+|ang|myċel}}, and {{m+|enm|wenche}} from {{m+|ang|wenċel}}), or at least related to it and/or to {{m|ang|bædan|bǣ̆dan|t=to defile}}, compare {{cog|goh|pad||hermaphrodite}}.

Alternatively, perhaps a loan from {{der|en|non|-}} into Middle English, compare {{cog|no|bad|pos=neuter noun|t=effort, trouble, fear}}, East {{cog|da|bad|pos=neuter noun|t=damage, destruction, fight}}, from the {{der|en|gem-pro|-}} noun {{m|gem-pro|*badą}}, whence also {{m+|gem-pro|*badōną|t=to frighten}}, {{cog|osx|undarbadōn|t=to frighten}}, {{cog|nn|bada|t=to weigh down, press}}; ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰedʰ-||to bend, press, push, oppress|id=press}}.<ref>{{R:gem:EDPG|*badōjan-|47}}</ref> {{fcog|fa|بد|tr=bad}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|worse,er<l:nonstandard>,more<l:nonstandard>|sup=worst,est<l:nonstandard>,most<l:nonstandard>}}

# Of [[low]] [[quality]].
#: {{syn|en|cruddy|lousy|shoddy|Thesaurus:low-quality}}
#: {{ux|en|That movie was really '''bad'''!}}
# [[inaccurate|Inaccurate]]; [[incorrect]].
#: {{ux|en|A '''bad''' guess.}}
#: {{ux|en|This sentence has '''bad''' grammar!}}
#: {{ux|en|He speaks '''bad''' German!}}
# [[unfavorable|Unfavorable]]; [[negative]]; not [[good]].
#: {{syn|en|unfavorable|negative|Thesaurus:bad}}
#: {{ux|en|Hiring practice is very '''bad''' in this company.}}
#: {{ux|en|The weather looks pretty '''bad''' right now.}}
#: {{ux|en|You have very '''bad''' grades.}}
#: {{ux|en|He is in a '''bad''' mood.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=10|passage=He looked round the poor room, at the distempered walls, and the '''bad''' engravings in meretricious frames, the crinkly paper and wax flowers on the chiffonier; and he thought of a room like Father Bryan's, with panelling, with cut glass, with tulips in silver pots, such a room as he had hoped to have for his own.}}
# Not [[suitable]] or [[fitting]].
#: {{syn|en|inappropriate|unfit|Thesaurus:unsuitable}}
#: {{ux|en|Do you think it is a '''bad''' idea to confront him directly?}}
# Not [[appropriate]], of [[manners]] etc.
#: {{ux|en|It is '''bad''' manners to talk with your mouth full.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=7|passage=“{{...}} if you call my duds a ‘livery’ again there'll be trouble. It's '''bad''' enough to go around togged out like a life saver on a drill day, but I can stand that 'cause I'm paid for it. What I won't stand is to have them togs called a livery. {{...}}”}}
# Harmful, especially [[unhealthy]]; liable to cause health problems.
#: {{syn|en|unhealthful|unwholesome|Thesaurus:harmful}}
#: {{ux|en|Lard is '''bad''' for you. Smoking is '''bad''' for you, too. Grapes are '''bad''' for dogs but not for humans.}}
# {{lb|en|chiefly applied to a person's state of health}} [[sickly|Sickly]], [[unhealthy]], [[unwell]].
#: {{syn|en|ill|poorly|sickly|Thesaurus:ill}}
#: {{ux|en|Joe's in a '''bad''' way; he can't even get out of bed.}}
#: {{ux|en|I went to the hospital to see how my grandfather was doing. Unfortunately, he's in a '''bad''' state.}}
#: {{ux|en|I've had a '''bad''' back since the accident.}}
# The injured or weak one of a pair of body parts, where the other one is healthy.
#: {{ux|en|I accidentally put my weight on my '''bad''' leg and fell over.}}
# {{lb|en|often|childish}} Not behaving; behaving badly; [[misbehaving]]; [[mischievous]] or [[disobedient]].
#: {{usex|en|Stop being '''bad''', or you will get a spanking!}}
#* {{quote-book|en|format=comic|author=Tom Armstrong|title=Marvin|date=Aug 28 2014|passage=I can tell that new kid at our daycare is trouble {{...}} He's picking out his favorite corner to stand in when he's '''bad'''.}}
# [[tricky|Tricky]]; [[stressful]]; [[unpleasant]].
#: {{syn|en|foul|loathsome|Thesaurus:unpleasant}}
#: {{ux|en|Divorce is usually a '''bad''' experience for everybody involved.}}
# {{lb|en|sometimes|childish}} [[evil|Evil]]; [[wicked]].
#: {{syn|en|vile|vicious|Thesaurus:evil}}
#: {{ux|en|Be careful. There are '''bad''' people in the world.}}
# [[faulty|Faulty]]; not [[functional]].
#: {{syn|en|inoperative|Thesaurus:out of order}}
#: {{ux|en|I had a '''bad''' headlight.}}
# {{lb|en|of food}} {{l|en|spoiled|Spoiled}}, [[rotten]], [[overripe]].
#: {{syn|en|rotten|Thesaurus:rotten}}
#: {{ux|en|These apples have gone '''bad'''.}}
# {{lb|en|of breath}} {{l|en|malodorous|Malodorous}}; [[foul]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:malodorous}}
#: {{ux|en|[[bad breath|'''Bad''' breath]] is not pleasant for anyone.}}
# [[false|False]]; [[counterfeit]]; [[illegitimate]].
#: {{syn|en|fake|spurious|Thesaurus:fake}}
#: {{ux|en|They were caught trying to pass '''bad''' coinage.}}
# [[unskilled|Unskilled]]; of limited [[ability]]; not [[good]].
#: {{syn|en|bungling|inept|Thesaurus:unskilled}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm pretty '''bad''' at speaking French.}}
#: {{ux|en|He's a '''bad''' gardener; everything he tries to grow ends up dying.}}
# Of [[poor]] physical [[appearance]].
#: {{syn|en|repulsive|unsightly|Thesaurus:ugly}}
#: {{ux|en|I look really '''bad''' whenever I get less than seven hours of sleep.}}
#: {{ux|en|I don't look '''bad''' in this dress, do I?}}
#: {{ux|en|I have such '''bad''' skin!}}
# {{lb|en|of a|need, want, or pain}} [[severe|Severe]], [[urgent]].
#: {{syn|en|dire|Thesaurus:urgent}}
#: {{ux|en|He is in '''bad''' need of a haircut.}}
# {{lb|en|preceded by {{m|en|feel}}}} [[regretful|Regretful]], [[guilty]], or [[ashamed]].
#: {{ux|en|I feel so '''bad''' for betraying him!}}
# {{lb|en|of a word, speech, or writing}} [[vulgar|Vulgar]], [[obscene]], or [[blasphemous]].
#: {{ux|en|Don't you dare speak to me with that '''bad''' language!}}
# Not [[worth it]].
#: {{ux|en|The expensive purse was a '''bad''' buy.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} Causing a problem rendering the current task impossible.
#: {{ux|en|'''Bad''' device, could not connect.}}

#: {{ux|en|The sacked quarterback was hurting '''bad'''. His back ached so '''bad''' that he had to [[lie down]].}}
# {{lb|en|intensifier}} [[badly|Badly]]; [[severe]]ly, [[extreme]]ly, [[passionate]]ly, [[eager]]ly.
#: {{ux|en|Please come back, baby. I miss you so '''bad'''!}}

=====Usage notes=====
* When placed after the main verb, use of ''bad'' as an intensifier is often more accepted than ''badly''. Compare:
** {{bad||I '''bad''' need to eat.}}  {{good||I '''badly''' need to eat.  }}
** {{qmark||I need '''bad''' to eat.}}  {{good||I need '''badly''' to eat.  }}
** {{good||I need to eat '''bad'''.}} {{qmark||I need to eat '''badly'''.}}
* It is also common  in certain set expressions, such as {{m|en|bad off}}, which may be perceived as an extended form of the adjective ''bad'' rather than the adverb ''bad ~ badly'' modifying the adjective [[off]].
* See also {{m|en|good#Usage_notes_2|good (adverb) § Usage notes}}.
